en: Taal Volcano's Main Crater Lake famously contained Vulcan Point, creating an island in a lake on an island in a lake.
Palawan is home to the Philippine mouse-deer, the world's smallest hoofed mammal, which stands only about twenty centimeters tall.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is so unique that its lower portion flows directly into the sea and experiences tidal bores.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is so remote that it is only accessible to divers via liveaboard boats for three months yearly.
If the stone walls of the Banaue Rice Terraces were laid end-to-end, they would stretch halfway around the globe.
The island province of Camiguin famously has seven volcanoes, meaning it actually has more volcanoes than it has municipalities.
The Philippines holds the second-largest gold deposit in the world, with the massive Didipio mine in Nueva Vizcaya producing significant copper and gold.
The Callao Cave in Cagayan features a massive naturally formed limestone chamber shaped exactly like a cathedral, complete with a stone altar.
The Philippine Trench, located within the Philippine Sea, plunges to a staggering depth of over ten thousand meters.
Found in the rainforests of Luzon and Mindanao, the Rafflesia produces the world's largest individual flower, which can weigh up to eleven kilograms.
The tiny Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has eyes larger than its brain and can rotate its head a full 180 degrees.
Bohol's famous Chocolate Hills consist of over one thousand perfectly cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
